short: A zero-rated supply is a taxable sale where the value-added tax rate is set to zero percent, allowing the seller to claim back the tax paid on their business expenses.
metaTitle: What is a Zero-Rated Supply? · Paper & Pen
metaDescription: A zero-rated supply is a taxable sale with a zero percent tax rate, allowing you to recover the input VAT paid on your business expenses.
definition:
When you sell goods or services, your local tax authority determines the applicable value-added tax rate. A zero-rated supply is a taxable transaction where the government sets the tax rate at exactly zero percent. This often applies to essential items like basic food, healthcare, or exports.

The most critical feature of a zero-rated supply is that it remains a taxable sale. Because you are making taxable sales, you have the right to recover the input VAT you paid on your business purchases. This is the main difference between zero-rated and exempt supplies. If your sales are exempt, you cannot claim back your input tax. By charging zero percent to your customer, you keep their costs low while protecting your own profit margins by recovering the tax on your expenses.

how.title: How Zero-rated supply works
how.body:
The process begins when you purchase materials or services to run your business. Your suppliers charge you standard input VAT on these purchases, which you record in your accounting system. Next, you manufacture your product or prepare your service for sale. When you invoice your customer for a qualifying zero-rated item, you apply a tax rate of zero percent. The customer pays no tax on that specific transaction.

At the end of your tax period, you file your tax return. You report the total value of your zero-rated sales. Then, you declare the input VAT you paid on your business expenses. Because your sales are zero-rated rather than exempt, the tax authority refunds the input tax you paid, or credits it against other tax liabilities.
items: You purchase business supplies and pay standard input VAT to your vendors.
You sell qualifying goods or services to your customers.
You issue a tax invoice showing a zero percent tax rate.
You report the zero-rated sales value on your periodic tax return.
You claim a full refund for the input VAT paid on your expenses.

example.title: Worked example
example.body:
Global Export Traders buys packaging materials for 1,000 plus a 5 percent standard input VAT, paying 1,050 in total. The 50 is their input tax. They use these materials to pack goods for export, which their tax authority classifies as a zero-rated supply.

They sell the exported goods for 4,000. Because the sale is zero-rated, they charge 0 percent tax, making the total invoice 4,000. When filing their tax return, they report 0 in output VAT and 50 in input VAT. Since zero-rated suppliers can recover input tax, the tax authority refunds the 50 to Global Export Traders.

matters:
Understanding zero-rated supplies is vital for your cash flow and pricing strategy. If you mistakenly treat a zero-rated sale as an exempt supply, you will lose the opportunity to recover the input VAT paid on your overheads. This directly reduces your net profit margin.

Conversely, applying a zero rate correctly ensures your goods remain competitively priced for your customers while you recoup your tax costs. Using a system like Paper & Pen, which creates invoices and tracks stock, helps you apply the correct tax codes to every item so your tax returns are accurate and your refunds are secure.

faqs.q: What is the difference between zero-rated and exempt supplies?
faqs.a: The decisive difference is your ability to recover input tax. If you sell zero-rated goods, the transaction is taxable at zero percent, and you can claim back the VAT paid on your business expenses. If you sell exempt goods, the transaction falls outside the tax system entirely, and you cannot recover any input VAT.

faqs.q: Do I need to issue a tax invoice for zero-rated sales?
faqs.a: Yes, you must usually issue a formal tax invoice for zero-rated sales. Because these transactions are legally taxable supplies, tax authorities require proper documentation. Your invoice must clearly show the net amount, the zero percent tax rate, and the total amount. This documentation proves to the government why no output tax was collected.

faqs.q: Do zero-rated sales count towards the VAT registration threshold?
faqs.a: Yes, zero-rated sales generally count towards your mandatory registration threshold. Even though the tax rate is zero, these are still classified as taxable supplies. You must monitor your total turnover, including all standard and zero-rated sales, to determine when you are legally required to register with your local tax authority.
